transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Well, what brings me in is that I just keep dodging anything that even smells like my old job. I mean, office buildings, security talks, networking events near the work sites... I just avoid them entirely. And if people start asking about the day it happened, I just... I make some excuse and get out of there.
Do unwanted memories of what happened at your old job ever suddenly pop into your mind?

Yes, they do. Out of nowhere, really. I'll just be washing the dishes, or maybe driving past a warehouse gate, and suddenly... the whole scene just pops right back into my head. It's so sharp. I can actually hear the panic in people's voices again, and my chest gets all tight, just like I'm right back there when it happened.
Since that incident, have you been feeling constantly on guard or easily startled?

Yes, I definitely feel on guard. It's... well, whenever I walk into a meeting room, or even just a restaurant, I always notice the exits first. I catch myself watching people's hands, just to see what they're doing. And I always make sure to pick a seat where nobody can come up behind me. I just need to know exactly what's going on around me at all times.
Have you been having nightmares about what happened at your old job?

Yes, I have been having them. It's... well, most nights I just lie there. I feel tired, but my brain is completely wired. And when I do finally fall asleep, I wake up from these dreams. It's always the same kind of things—radios crackling, people shouting. Then I'm just awake before daylight, and I feel like I haven't rested at all.
Since this started, have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I'd say so. Things like... well, listening to salsa music, or painting, or even just cooking Sunday dinner. Those things really used to lift me up. But now... I just kind of go through the motions. I still do them sometimes, but that good feeling just doesn't come the way it used to.
Since that incident, have you been blaming yourself for what happened?

No, not really. I mean... I know what happened wasn't my fault. It was just a terrible situation. I don't put the blame on myself for it happening, I just... well, I just have to deal with the aftermath, I guess. But no, I don't blame myself.
Since the incident, have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

No, I wouldn't say I feel depressed. I mean, I'm definitely exhausted from not sleeping, and I don't have the energy for my hobbies like I said, but... I don't feel sad or down in the dumps most days. It's more just feeling drained and kind of on edge, rather than depressed.
Did the incident at your old job involve a situation where you thought you or someone else might be killed or seriously injured?

No, it wasn't really like that. I mean... I didn't think anyone was going to die or get physically hurt. It wasn't that kind of physical danger. It was just a really terrible situation to go through, but... no, I didn't think anyone would be killed or seriously injured.
Did these symptoms start within 3 months after what happened at your old job?

I'm honestly not sure about the exact timeline. I mean... things just sort of blurred together after I left that job. I couldn't tell you for certain if it all started within those first three months, or if it took a bit longer for the exhaustion and the edginess to really set in. I just don't have a clear start date for it.
Do you feel intense fear specifically when you are near office buildings or work-related places?
No, not really. I mean, I don't get terrified just from being near an office building or anything like that. It's not a specific fear of those places.
Have these symptoms made it hard for you to work or handle your usual day-to-day responsibilities?

Yes, they have. It's definitely affecting my daily life and my career. I've actually turned down job interviews recently, and I had to stop taking on my usual volunteer responsibilities. I just... I can't reliably get through a meeting or a site visit without feeling like I need to shut down or just leave the room. And it's not just work. Even with my family and the mentoring circles I'm part of, I'm just less present. People have started noticing that I pull back now, instead of stepping up and leading the way I used to. So, yes, it's making things very difficult.
Have these symptoms been going on for more than 6 months?
Yes, definitely longer than six months. It's... well, this has all been going on since I was fired right after that armed incident. So, looking back, that was about a year and seven months ago now.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different parts of your life, not just about what happened at your old job?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm not sitting around worrying about my bills or my health or... just everyday things. I've always been a pretty practical person. It's really just... my stress is all tied back to that incident and losing my job. That's what messes with my head, not just a general worry about everything else in my life.
